newsitem.title: GERMANY: Duisenberg - any EMU delay could be permanent delay.
newsitem.headline: Duisenberg - any EMU delay could be permanent delay.

text.p: Dutch Central Bank head Wim Duisenberg said on Wednesday any delay to European Monetary Union (EMU) could turn out to be permanent and also said he could not foresee the EMU starting without Germany.
Asked whether or not the EMU's 1999 start could be put back if countries missed the Maastricht Treaty convergence criteria this year he said: "I fear that a delay would lead to a permanent delay."
Duisenberg added that Maastricht does not foresee a postponement of the launch and, although some legal experts say such a delay was possible, he considered that to be very risky.

"I regard that personally as very dangerous. I believe that it would then be necessary to renegotiate the Treaty and for it to be ratified by all 15 parliaments (in the European Union)," Duisenberg said.
Some countries would be bound to seek changes to the structure of monetary union. Duisenberg added that "there would be no point" in starting monetary union without Germany.

Germany has said that its national debt will rise this year above the threshold of 60 percent of gross domestic product (GDP) specified in the Maastricht Treaty and Finance Minister Theo Waigel is struggling to reduce the budget deficit below three percent of GDP, while handicapped by record post-war unemployment.
In a speech, Duisenberg said it was vital for countries wanting to join EMU to achieve lasting convergence to the Maastricht targets for the planned euro currency to be stable.
Duisenberg will take over as head of the European Monetary Institute this summer and is tipped to take over the European Central Bank in Frankfurt, which will run monetary policy.
